results.title: coverforest: Conformal Predictions with Random Forest in Python
results.content: We present coverforest, a Python package that implements efficient conformal prediction methods specifically optimized for random forests. coverforest  supports both regression and classification tasks through various conformal prediction methods, including split conformal, CV+, Jackknife+-after-bootstrap, and adaptive prediction sets. Recent conformal prediction methods like CV+ and Jackknife+-after-bootstrap (J+ab) rely on out-of-fold and out-of-bag calculations—techniques extensively studied in ensemble learning, particularly in random forests [1]. Even though these implementations are only for in-sample out-of-bag calculations, we can adapt the technique for train-test cross-conformity score calculations, enabling faster conformal predictions with CV+ and J+ab. coverforest implements several recent advances in conformal prediction, including split conformal, CV+ and J+ab for regression, and adaptive prediction set (APS) with split conformal, CV+, and J+ab for classification. Random forest is our model of choice for three reasons 1) they have consistently demonstrated good performance on tabular data [2], 2) they can be trained with missing data, and 3) trees are very fast to train in parallel, making them attractive for cross-conformal predictions like CV+ and J+ab. Experimental results show that coverforest’s conformal training and prediction of random forests are faster than an existing implementation by 2–9 times faster. In Table 1, we compare coverage guarantees and computational costs across different conformal prediction methods for random forests. The methods with the APS score, however, have notably long prediction times due to the pairwise comparisons between train and test conformity scores across all classes. {minted}[ frame=lines, framesep=2mm, baselinestretch=1.2, fontsize=]python clf = CoverForestClassifier( n\_estimators=400, method="bootstrap", k\_init=0, lambda\_init=0 ) clf.fit(X\_train, y\_train) y\_pred, y\_sets = clf.predict(X\_test, alpha=0.05) avg\_set\_size = average\_set\_size\_loss(y\_test, y\_sets) coverage = classification\_coverage\_score(y\_test, y\_sets) # y\_pred[:5] = [2, 8, 2, 6, 6] # y\_sets[:5] = [array([2]), array([2, 5, 8, 9]), # array([2]), array([6]), array([6])] # avg\_set\_size = 1.761 # coverage = 0.968 Compared to the CV+ method, J+ab produces prediction sets with a larger average with practically the same coverage. Since each tree in CV+ is trained on 90% of the data, we accordingly set both J+ab and split conformal methods to use 900 trees to maintain consistency in the learning capacity. For coverforest and MAPIE, we train a random forest and make conformal predictions using CV+, J+ab and split conformal methods, all with the APS score.

results.content: # Title:coverforest: Conformal Predictions with Random Forest in Python. View a PDF of the paper titled coverforest: Conformal Predictions with Random Forest in Python, by Panisara Meehinkong and 1 other authors. > Abstract:Conformal prediction provides a framework for uncertainty quantification, specifically in the forms of prediction intervals and sets with distribution-free guaranteed coverage. While recent cross-conformal techniques such as CV+ and Jackknife+-after-bootstrap achieve better data efficiency than traditional split conformal methods, they incur substantial computational costs due to required pairwise comparisons between training and test samples' out-of-bag scores. Observing that these methods naturally extend from ensemble models, particularly random forests, we leverage existing optimized random forest implementations to enable efficient cross-conformal predictions. > We present coverforest, a Python package that implements efficient conformal prediction methods specifically optimized for random forests. coverforest supports both regression and classification tasks through various conformal prediction methods, including split conformal, CV+, Jackknife+-after-bootstrap, and adaptive prediction sets. Our experiments demonstrate that coverforest's predictions achieve the desired level of coverage.
